symptom: The pricing page matched Portal V2 and SaaS entitlements, but parity was protected mainly by phrase-level assertions instead of a direct comparison with the canonical server-side entitlement seed.
root_cause: Commercial pricing copy and canonical SaaS entitlement records live in different artifacts.
Existing tests validated selected phrases but did not fail when numeric limits, agent mode, advisory allowance or governance entitlements drifted from the Supabase seed.
fix: Add a regression test that parses the canonical SaaS plan and entitlement seed directly from the Supabase migration.
Compare Control, Scale and Enterprise limits and operating modes against the actual pricing-page product cards.
Lock monthly and yearly pricing copy to the canonical seeded plan prices.
prevention: Commercial product promises must be mechanically checked against server-side entitlements.
A future change to sources, freshness, agent mode, organisations, SSO, audit trail or advisory time must update both entitlement truth and customer-facing pricing copy in one lineage.
All paid plans keep the same intelligence core; tier differentiation remains scale, freshness, automation, governance and advisory envelope.
evidence: supabase/migrations/20260920101730_saas_checkout_entitlements_20260920.sql is the canonical seeded entitlement source.
tests/pricing-entitlement-source-parity.test.mjs reads that source and verifies prijzen.html directly.
